claim: A proactive face watermark trained on one collection of faces and a fixed set of deepfake generators keeps working, without retraining, on a deepfake generator it never trained against and on a different face collection. Each kind of generalisation is judged separately. Supported only if the source identifier is recovered with a lower bit error rate than the strongest earlier proactive-forensics method at matched resolution, both on the held-out generator and averaged over generators on the unseen faces, while PSNR and SSIM on the unseen faces are no lower than the best earlier watermark.

experiments: Train the watermarking system. Setup: CelebA-HQ (30k faces, official splits) at 128x128 and 256x256. Each image gets a 152-number mark: 68 face-alignment landmarks (136 coordinates) plus a 16-bit identifier derived from a hash of the file name. Training is two-stage: first against ordinary processing (resize, blur, median filter, two JPEG variants), then against four face-swap/reenactment generators (SimSwap, UniFace, CSCS, StarGAN-v2), keeping InfoSwap unseen for testing; one manipulation per batch, with another batch image as the swap source.

Generalise to a deepfake generator excluded from training. Setup: InfoSwap is applied only at test time. Result: identifier BER 0.22% (128px) and 0.84% (256px), landmark error 1.5 and 3.9 px; the best earlier InfoSwap BERs are 3.35% (LampMark, 128px) and 2.31% (DiffMark, 256px).

Generalise to a face dataset never seen in training. Setup: apply the CelebA-HQ model unchanged to 2,000 random LFW images (different identities and capture conditions). Result: PSNR/SSIM 39.56 dB / 0.97 (128px) and 40.68 / 0.98 (256px); identifier BER averaged over the five generators 4.06% and 2.76% versus 4.66% and 4.50% for the best earlier method (DiffMark); landmark error 1.8 and 4.2 px.
